        print(f"  {N:5d} | {str(w):19s} | {w is not None and w > N}")
    print()
    print("Hence no algorithm inspecting only x_0..x_N and y_0..y_N can decide")
    print("the order: it is decidable eventually, and never uniformly.")


def demo_ivt() -> None:
    line("5.  The intermediate value theorem: approximate, exact, and bracketing")

    # f(x) = x^2 - 2 on [1, 2]: 4-Lipschitz there, slope bound 2 (since
    # f(y) - f(x) = (y+x)(y-x) >= 2(y-x) for 1 <= x <= y <= 2).
    def f(x: float) -> float:
        return x * x - 2.0

    a, b = 1.0, 2.0
    omega = lambda e: e / 4.0  # 4-Lipschitz on [1, 2]
    c = 2.0                    # slope bound
    root = math.sqrt(2.0)

    print("f(x) = x^2 - 2 on [1, 2];  modulus omega(eps) = eps/4;  slope bound c = 2.")
    print("Exact root:  sqrt(2) = %.12f" % root)
    print()
    print("Approximate IVT (value accuracy eps):")
    print("     eps    |    N   |     x found    |    |f(x)|    | <= eps?")
    print("  " + "-" * 68)
    for eps in [1e-1, 1e-2, 1e-3, 1e-4]:
        N, x, fx = approximate_ivt(f, a, b, omega, eps)
        print(f"  {eps:.1e} | {N:6d} | {x:.12f} | {abs(fx):.3e} | {abs(fx) <= eps}")
    print()

    print("Exact IVT via the root modulus  delta -> omega(c*delta),")
    print("using the sharp conversion  |x - r| <= |f(x)| / c :")
    print("    delta   |    N   |     x found    |   |x - r|   | <= delta?")
    print("  " + "-" * 68)
    for delta in [1e-1, 1e-2, 1e-3, 1e-4]:
        N, x = constructive_ivt(f, a, b, omega, c, delta)
        print(f"  {delta:.1e} | {N:6d} | {x:.12f} | {abs(x-root):.3e} "
              f"| {abs(x - root) <= delta}")
    print()

    print("Sharpness of the constant eps/c:  for f(x) = c*x on [-1, 1] with root 0,")
    print("the point x = eps/c has |f(x)| = eps and |x - 0| = eps/c EXACTLY.")
    for cc, ee in [(1.0, 0.5), (2.0, 0.25), (0.5, 0.5)]:
        xx = ee / cc
        print(f"    c = {cc:4.2f}, eps = {ee:4.2f}:  |f(x)| = {abs(cc*xx):.4f},"
              f"  |x - r| = {abs(xx):.4f},  eps/c = {ee/cc:.4f}")
    print("  So no factor kappa < 1 can improve the bound.")
    print()

    print("Bracketing (NO non-degeneracy hypothesis): the sign-change search")
    print("lands within one mesh of a genuine root.")
    print("       N |  mesh (b-a)/N |  |x - r|   | within one mesh?")
    print("  " + "-" * 62)
    for N in [8, 64, 512, 4096]:
        k = grid_search(f, a, b, N)
        x = grid(a, b, N, k)
        mesh = (b - a) / N
        print(f"  {N:6d} | {mesh:.10f} | {abs(x-root):.3e} | {abs(x-root) <= mesh}")


def demo_shelf() -> None:
    line("6.  The shelf family: the exact IVT has no effective solution")
    print("S_t(x) = min(x - 1, max(t, x - 2))  on [0, 3],  1-Lipschitz for every t,")
    print("with S_t(0) <= 0 <= S_t(3).  The approximate IVT applies uniformly in t.")
    print()
    print("      t     | exact root(s) | approx root (N=3000) | |S_t| at that point")
    print("  " + "-" * 76)
    for t in [1.0, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0, -0.001, -0.01, -0.1, -1.0]:
        N = 3000
        k = grid_search(lambda x, t=t: shelf(t, x), 0.0, 3.0, N)
        x = grid(0.0, 3.0, N, k)
        exact = "all of [1,2]" if t == 0.0 else f"{shelf_exact_root(t):.4f}"
        print(f"  {t:+9.4f} | {exact:>13s} | {x:20.6f} "
              f"| {abs(shelf(t, x)):.3e}")
    print()
    print("The APPROXIMATE root is found effectively for every t (all |S_t| tiny).")
    print("The EXACT root jumps from 1 to 2 as t crosses 0 -- no continuous rule")
    print("can track it, and since every constructive function is continuous, no")
    print("constructive rule can either.")
    print()
    print("Quantitative failure: EVERY selector, continuous or not, has")
    print("oscillation at least 1 on every window |t| <= eta.")
    print("      eta    | r(+min(eta,1)) | r(-min(eta,1)) | oscillation >= ")
    print("  " + "-" * 68)
    for eta in [1.0, 0.1, 1e-3, 1e-6, 1e-12]:
        s = min(eta, 1.0)
        lo, hi = shelf_exact_root(s), shelf_exact_root(-s)
        print(f"  {eta:.1e} | {lo:14.1f} | {hi:14.1f} | {abs(hi-lo):.1f}")
    print()
    print("And the missing hypothesis is identified exactly: S_0 is constant on")
    print("[1, 2], so it admits no positive slope bound --")
    print(f"    S_0(1) = {shelf(0.0, 1.0)},  S_0(2) = {shelf(0.0, 2.0)}"
          "  =>  c * 1 <= 0.")


def demo_dip() -> None:
    line("7.  Local non-constancy is not enough")
    print("D_eta(x) = min(x - 1, |x - 3| + eta)  on [0, 4]:  1-Lipschitz, unique")
    print("root x = 1, local non-constancy with the explicit modulus nu(h) = h/8.")
    print()
    print("     delta  |    eta    |  |D(3)|  |  nu(delta)/2 |  distance 3 to root")
    print("  " + "-" * 74)
    for delta in [1.0, 0.5, 0.1, 0.01]:
        eta = delta / 32.0
        print(f"  {delta:8.4f} | {eta:9.6f} | {abs(dip(eta, 3.0)):.6f} "
              f"| {delta/16:12.6f} | {abs(3.0 - 1.0):.1f}")
    print()
    print("The value at x = 3 is as small as one likes, yet x = 3 is at distance 2")
    print("from the only root.  So 'small |f|' does NOT imply 'near a root' under")
    print("local non-constancy alone: the slope bound is genuinely needed.")
    print()
    print("Verification of local non-constancy nu(h) = h/8 by sampling intervals:")
    eta = 0.01
    worst = None
    for i in range(400):
        p = 4.0 * i / 400.0
        for h in [0.05, 0.2, 1.0]:
            q = min(4.0, p + h)
            if q - p < h - 1e-12:
                continue
            best = max(abs(dip(eta, p + j * (q - p) / 60.0)) for j in range(61))
            ratio = best / (h / 8.0)
            if worst is None or ratio < worst:
                worst = ratio
    print(f"  minimum observed  max|D| / nu(h)  over sampled intervals: {worst:.3f}")
    print("  (>= 1 everywhere, as the theorem asserts)")

          f"   exact: {q - p == Q(2,3)**10}")

        print(f"    n = {n}: [{str(p):>11s}, {str(q):>11s}]   width = {q - p}"
              f"   contains 1/2: {p < c <= q}")
    p, q = fast[10]
    print(f"    n = 10: width = {float(q-p):.8f} <= (3/5)^10 = {float(Q(3,5)**10):.8f}"
          f"   holds: {q - p <= Q(3,5)**10}")
    print()

    print("Contraction factors  max(beta, 1 - alpha):")
    print("     alpha  |  beta   | factor  | factor^10  | note")
    print("  " + "-" * 68)
    schemes = [
        (Q(1, 3), Q(2, 3), "Bishop's trisection"),
        (Q(2, 5), Q(1, 2), "strictly faster"),
        (Q(9, 20), Q(1, 2), "closer to the barrier"),

    print(f"Every factor is strictly greater than 1/2: "
          f"{all(contraction_factor(a, b) > Q(1,2) for a, b, _ in schemes)}")
    print("but the infimum 1/2 is approached: taking alpha = 1/2 - t/2, beta = 1/2 + t/2")
    print("gives factor 1/2 + t/2, below 1/2 + eta for any eta > 0.")
    print()
    print("Oracle calls to reach accuracy tau, starting from width 1:")
    print("        tau    | trisection (2/3) | faster (3/5) | calls saved")
    print("  " + "-" * 66)
    for tau in [1e-3, 1e-6, 1e-9, 1e-12]:
        n23 = math.ceil(math.log(tau) / math.log(2 / 3))
        n35 = math.ceil(math.log(tau) / math.log(3 / 5))
        print(f"  {tau:.1e} | {n23:16d} | {n35:12d} | {n23 - n35:11d}")
    print()
    print("The reason 1/2 cannot be reached: a legitimate query needs alpha < beta,")
    print("so the 'true' region [0, beta] and the 'false' region [alpha, 1] overlap")
    print("in [alpha, beta].  That overlap is the price of the oracle's freedom to")

      "code": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Constructive Analysis: Bishop Reals, the Constructive IVT, and Located Suprema
==============================================================================

A self-contained numerical demonstration of the results in the accompanying
paper.  Everything below runs in exact rational arithmetic (``fractions.Fraction``)
wherever the mathematics is rational, so the numbers printed are the numbers
proved -- not floating-point approximations of them.

Contents
--------

      |x_m - x_n| <= 1/(m+1) + 1/(n+1),  and  |x_hat - x_n| <= 1/(n+1).

    (product), with the canonical bound B_x = ceil(|x_0|) + 2.
3.  A computable irrational: sqrt(2) via integer square roots.
4.  Constructive completeness: the shifted diagonal (x_{2n+1})_{2n+1}, and an
    explicit witness family showing the unshifted diagonal fails.
5.  The constructive order: positivity witnesses, cotransitivity by a single
    midpoint comparison, and the non-existence of a uniform witness bound.
6.  The approximate intermediate value theorem: the finite grid search, with
    the sharp root modulus eps/c and the hypothesis-free bracketing bound.
7.  Brouwerian counterexample: the shelf family S_t(x) = min(x-1, max(t, x-2))
    and the unit jump of every root selector at t = 0.
8.  Local non-constancy is insufficient: the dip function.
9.  Located suprema: trisection vs. the faster (2/5, 1/2) one-query search,
    the exact contraction law max(beta, 1-alpha), and the barrier 1/2.

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Callable, List, Optional, Tuple

Q = Fraction


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 1.  Bishop reals: regular sequences of rationals
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# A Bishop real is represented as a function n |-> x_n in Q, with the promise
#     |x_m - x_n| <= 1/(m+1) + 1/(n+1)   for all m, n.
Reg = Callable[[int], Q]


def err(n: int) -> Q:
    """The canonical error bar at index ``n``: the number 1/(n+1)."""
    return Q(1, n + 1)


def check_regular(x: Reg, upto: int = 40) -> bool:
    """Verify the regularity inequality for all index pairs below ``upto``."""
    for m in range(upto):
        for n in range(upto):
            if abs(x(m) - x(n)) > err(m) + err(n):
                return False
    return True


def of_rat(q: Q) -> Reg:
    """The Bishop real determined by a rational constant."""
    return lambda _n: q


def neg(x: Reg) -> Reg:
    """Negation; no index shift is required."""
    return lambda n: -x(n)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 2.  Computable arithmetic with Bishop's index shifts
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def add(x: Reg, y: Reg) -> Reg:
    """Sum, with Bishop's index shift n |-> 2n+1 (each summand to twice the
    required accuracy, so that the two halved error bars sum correctly)."""
    return lambda n: x(2 * n + 1) + y(2 * n + 1)


def bound(x: Reg) -> int:
    """Bishop's canonical bound  B_x = ceil(|x_0|) + 2, which dominates |x_n|
    for every n, because |x_n - x_0| <= 1/(n+1) + 1 <= 2."""
    return math.ceil(abs(x(0))) + 2


def mul(x: Reg, y: Reg) -> Reg:
    """Product, with index shift  n |-> (B_x + B_y)(n+1).  The shift must grow
    with the magnitudes because an error delta in a factor of size B becomes an
    error B*delta in the product."""
    m = bound(x) + bound(y)
    return lambda n: x(m * (n + 1)) * y(m * (n + 1))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 3.  A concrete computable irrational
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def sqrt_two(n: int) -> Q:
    """The n-th approximation of sqrt(2):  floor(sqrt(2(n+1)^2)) / (n+1).

    Pure integer arithmetic.  The estimate  s <= sqrt(2) m < s+1  for
    s = isqrt(2 m^2)  gives  |s/m - sqrt(2)| <= 1/m,  which is regularity with
    the canonical rate."""
    m = n + 1
    return Q(math.isqrt(2 * m * m), m)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 4.  Constructive completeness and the diagonal shift
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def diag_witness(k: int) -> Reg:
    """The k-th member of the family that separates the two diagonals:

        (x_k)_n = 1/(k+1) + (-1)^k / (n+1).

    Each member is regular and denotes the real 1/(k+1); the built-in wobble
    sits exactly at the edge of the permitted error, with a sign flipping in k.
    """
    sign = 1 if k % 2 == 0 else -1
    return lambda n: Q(1, k + 1) + sign * Q(1, n + 1)


def shifted_diagonal(family: Callable[[int], Reg]) -> Reg:
    """Bishop's limit construction:  L_n = (x_{2n+1})_{2n+1}."""
    return lambda n: family(2 * n + 1)(2 * n + 1)


def unshifted_diagonal(family: Callable[[int], Reg]) -> Reg:
    """The naive diagonal  n |-> (x_n)_n,  which need not be regular."""
    return lambda n: family(n)(n)


def first_regularity_violation(x: Reg, upto: int = 20) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int, Q, Q]]:
    """Return the first (m, n, observed gap, permitted gap) violating regularity."""
    for m in range(upto):
        for n in range(upto):
            gap = abs(x(m) - x(n))
            allowed = err(m) + err(n)
            if gap > allowed:
                return (m, n, gap, allowed)
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 5.  The constructive order
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def lt_witness(x: Reg, y: Reg, search: int = 500) -> Optional[int]:
    """Search for a witness index n for  x < y,  i.e. an n with
    x_n + 2/(n+1) < y_n.  A witness is a *certificate*, not a mere assertion:
    from it one reads off the rational lower bound gap_n(x, y) on y - x."""
    for n in range(search):
        if x(n) + 2 * err(n) < y(n):
            return n
    return None


def gap_at(x: Reg, y: Reg, n: int) -> Q:
    """The certified rational gap  g_n = y_n - x_n - 2/(n+1)."""
    return y(n) - x(n) - 2 * err(n)


def cotransitivity_index(g: Q) -> int:
    """The index m guaranteed by the cotransitivity theorem: any m with
    1/(m+1) <= g/8, i.e. m = ceil(8/g) - 1."""
    return max(0, math.ceil(Q(8, 1) / g) - 1)


def cotransitive_decide(x: Reg, y: Reg, z: Reg, n: int) -> Tuple[str, int]:
    """Given a witness index ``n`` for x < y, decide  x < z  or  z < y  by a
    single rational comparison of z_m against the midpoint (x_m + y_m)/2."""
    g = gap_at(x, y, n)
    if g <= 0:
        raise ValueError("index n is not a witness for x < y")
    m = cotransitivity_index(g)
    midpoint = (x(m) + y(m)) / 2
    if z(m) >= midpoint:
        return ("x < z", m)
    return ("z < y", m)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 6.  The intermediate value theorem
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def grid(a: float, b: float, N: int, k: int) -> float:
    """The k-th point of the uniform grid of N subintervals of [a, b]."""
    return a + k * (b - a) / N


def grid_search(f: Callable[[float], float], a: float, b: float, N: int) -> int:
    """The sign-change search: return the largest grid index k with f <= 0.

    This single index is simultaneously
      * an eps-approximate root whenever the mesh is at most omega(eps), and
      * within one mesh (b-a)/N of a genuine root, with no hypotheses at all.
    """
    best = 0
    for k in range(N + 1):
        if f(grid(a, b, N, k)) <= 0:
            best = k
    return best


def approximate_ivt(
    f: Callable[[float], float],
    a: float,
    b: float,
    omega: Callable[[float], float],
    eps: float,
) -> Tuple[int, float, float]:
    """Approximate IVT with explicit modulus.  Choose N with mesh <= omega(eps),
    run the grid search, and return (N, x, f(x)) with |f(x)| <= eps guaranteed."""
    N = max(1, math.ceil((b - a) / omega(eps)) + 1)
    k = grid_search(f, a, b, N)
    x = grid(a, b, N, k)
    return (N, x, f(x))


def constructive_ivt(
    f: Callable[[float], float],
    a: float,
    b: float,
    omega: Callable[[float], float],
    c: float,
    delta: float,
) -> Tuple[int, float]:
    """Exact IVT under a positive slope bound ``c``.  The modulus of the root is
    delta |-> omega(c * delta): run the grid search at value-accuracy c*delta and
    the returned point is within ``delta`` of the unique root."""
    N, x, _fx = approximate_ivt(f, a, b, omega, c * delta)
    return (N, x)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 7.  The shelf family (Brouwerian counterexample)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def shelf(t: float, x: float) -> float:
    """Bishop's shelf function  S_t(x) = min(x-1, max(t, x-2))  on [0, 3].

    1-Lipschitz for every t, with S_t(0) <= 0 <= S_t(3).  Its root is 1 for
    t > 0 and 2 for t < 0, so it teleports as t crosses zero."""
    return min(x - 1.0, max(t, x - 2.0))


def shelf_exact_root(t: float) -> float:
    """The exact root of S_t, which exists classically for every t."""
    if t > 0:
        return 1.0
    if t < 0:
        return 2.0
    return 1.0  # at t = 0 the whole interval [1, 2] consists of roots


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 8.  Local non-constancy is insufficient
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def dip(eta: float, x: float) -> float:
    """D_eta(x) = min(x - 1, |x - 3| + eta) on [0, 4].

    1-Lipschitz, unique root x = 1, satisfies local non-constancy with the
    explicit modulus nu(h) = h/8 -- and yet D_eta(3) = eta is arbitrarily small
    at distance 2 from the only root."""
    return min(x - 1.0, abs(x - 3.0) + eta)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 9.  Located suprema
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Oracle = Callable[[Q, Q], bool]


def located_iic(c: Q) -> Oracle:
    """A located datum for the half-line (-inf, c] with rational endpoint c:
    the decidable test  L(p, q) = (c <= q).

      * true  => q is an upper bound of the half-line;
      * false => q < c, so the member c itself exceeds p (since p < q < c).
    """
    return lambda _p, q: c <= q


def search_step(alpha: Q, beta: Q, L: Oracle, pq: Tuple[Q, Q]) -> Tuple[Q, Q]:
    """One step of the general one-query search with query fractions alpha < beta.
    On ``true`` keep the left beta-portion; on ``false`` the right (1-alpha)-portion."""
    p, q = pq
    w = q - p
    if L(p + alpha * w, p + beta * w):
        return (p, p + beta * w)
    return (p + alpha * w, q)


def search(alpha: Q, beta: Q, L: Oracle, a0: Q, b0: Q, n: int) -> List[Tuple[Q, Q]]:
    """The first ``n+1`` enclosures produced by the one-query search."""
    out = [(a0, b0)]
    for _ in range(n):
        out.append(search_step(alpha, beta, L, out[-1]))
    return out


def contraction_factor(alpha: Q, beta: Q) -> Q:
    """The exact worst-case contraction factor of a one-query scheme:
    max(beta, 1 - alpha)."""
    return max(beta, 1 - alpha)

def line(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 78)


def demo_regular_sequences() -> None:
    line("1.  Bishop reals: the index IS the error bar")
    print("A regular sequence satisfies  |x_m - x_n| <= 1/(m+1) + 1/(n+1),")
    print("from which  |x_hat - x_n| <= 1/(n+1)  follows by letting m -> infinity.")
    print()
    print("  n |   sqrt2_n     |  1/(n+1)   |  actual |sqrt2_n - sqrt2|")
    print("  " + "-" * 62)
    for n in [0, 1, 4, 9, 99, 999]:
        approx = sqrt_two(n)
        actual = abs(float(approx) - math.sqrt(2))
        print(f"{n:5d} | {str(approx):13s} | {float(err(n)):.6f} | {actual:.10f}")
    print()
    ok = check_regular(sqrt_two, upto=40)
    print(f"Regularity verified for all index pairs below 40:  {ok}")
    print(f"Certified values:  sqrt2_4 = {sqrt_two(4)},  sqrt2_99 = {sqrt_two(99)}")


def demo_arithmetic() -> None:
    line("2.  Computable arithmetic and Bishop's index shifts")
    x = sqrt_two
    y = of_rat(Q(3, 2))

    s = add(x, y)
    p = mul(x, x)

    print("Sum uses the shift n -> 2n+1; product uses n -> (B_x + B_y)(n+1).")
    print(f"Canonical bound of sqrt2:  B = ceil(|x_0|) + 2 = {bound(x)}")
    print(f"Canonical bound of 3/2:    B = ceil(|x_0|) + 2 = {bound(y)}")
    print()
    print("  n |  (sqrt2 + 3/2)_n   | error vs true      |  (sqrt2 * sqrt2)_n  | err vs 2")
    print("  " + "-" * 76)
    true_sum = math.sqrt(2) + 1.5
    for n in [0, 2, 9, 49]:
        sv, pv = s(n), p(n)
        print(
            f"{n:5d} | {str(sv)[:18]:18s} | {abs(float(sv) - true_sum):.10f} "
            f"| {str(pv)[:19]:19s} | {abs(float(pv) - 2.0):.10f}"
        )
    print()
    print(f"Sum regular (checked to index 40):     {check_regular(s, 40)}")
    print(f"Product regular (checked to index 25): {check_regular(p, 25)}")
    print()
    print("Note the price of multiplication: to get accuracy 1/(n+1) in the product")
    print(f"one must evaluate each factor at index {bound(x)+bound(x)}(n+1) -- the precision")
    print("blow-up is linear in the magnitude bound.  That is what makes the")
    print("constructive reals a ring: the bound must be computed from the data.")


def demo_completeness() -> None:
    line("3.  Constructive completeness: why the diagonal must be shifted")
    print("Witness family:   (x_k)_n = 1/(k+1) + (-1)^k / (n+1),   x_k denotes 1/(k+1).")
    print("These reals form a regular sequence of reals converging to 0.")
    print()

    naive = unshifted_diagonal(diag_witness)
    good = shifted_diagonal(diag_witness)

    print("Unshifted diagonal  n -> (x_n)_n :")
    for n in range(4):
        print(f"    n = {n}:  {naive(n)}")
    v = first_regularity_violation(naive, upto=8)
    assert v is not None
    m, n, observed, allowed = v
    print(f"  --> REGULARITY FAILS at (m, n) = ({m}, {n}):")
    print(f"      observed |difference| = {observed},  permitted = {allowed}")
    print("      The naive diagonal is not a real number at all.")
    print()
    print("Bishop's shifted diagonal  n -> (x_{2n+1})_{2n+1} :")
    for n in range(4):
        print(f"    n = {n}:  {good(n)}   (|value| <= 1/(n+1) = {err(n)}:"
              f" {abs(good(n)) <= err(n)})")
    print(f"  --> regular (checked to index 40): {check_regular(good, 40)}")
    print(f"  --> converges to the correct limit 0;  L_50 = {float(good(50)):+.6f}")
    print()
    print("Doubling the index halves the wobble, and that is exactly enough:")
    print("each of the two chains in the proof consumes one half.")


def demo_order() -> None:
    line("4.  The constructive order: witnesses, cotransitivity, non-uniformity")

    x = of_rat(Q(0))
    y = of_rat(Q(1, 3))
    n = lt_witness(x, y)
    assert n is not None
    g = gap_at(x, y, n)
    print(f"x = 0,  y = 1/3.   First witness index for x < y:  n = {n}")
    print(f"  certified rational gap  g = y_n - x_n - 2/(n+1) = {g}")
    print(f"  so  y - x >= {g}  is proved, not merely asserted.")
    print()

    print("Cotransitivity: one midpoint comparison decides x < z or z < y.")
    m = cotransitivity_index(g)
    print(f"  computed index  m = ceil(8/g) - 1 = {m}")
    for name, z in [("z = 1/10", of_rat(Q(1, 10))),
                    ("z = 1/4 ", of_rat(Q(1, 4))),
                    ("z = 0   ", of_rat(Q(0)))]:
        verdict, mm = cotransitive_decide(x, y, z, n)
        print(f"    {name} -> decided '{verdict}' at index {mm}")
    print("  (Both alternatives may be true; the test always returns a true one.)")
    print()

    print("No uniform witness bound: for x = 0, y = 1/(N+1) the inequality holds")
    print("but no index n <= N certifies it.")
    print()
    print("     N | first witness index | is it > N?")
    print("     " + "-" * 44)
    for N in [1, 3, 10, 30, 100]:
        yN = of_rat(Q(1, N + 1))
        w = lt_witness(of_rat(Q(0)), yN, search=4000)
        print(f"  {N:5d} | {str(w):19s} | {w is not None and w > N}")
    print()
    print("Hence no algorithm inspecting only x_0..x_N and y_0..y_N can decide")
    print("the order: it is decidable eventually, and never uniformly.")


def demo_ivt() -> None:
    line("5.  The intermediate value theorem: approximate, exact, and bracketing")

    # f(x) = x^2 - 2 on [1, 2]: 4-Lipschitz there, slope bound 2 (since
    # f(y) - f(x) = (y+x)(y-x) >= 2(y-x) for 1 <= x <= y <= 2).
    def f(x: float) -> float:
        return x * x - 2.0

    a, b = 1.0, 2.0
    omega = lambda e: e / 4.0  # 4-Lipschitz on [1, 2]
    c = 2.0                    # slope bound
    root = math.sqrt(2.0)

    print("f(x) = x^2 - 2 on [1, 2];  modulus omega(eps) = eps/4;  slope bound c = 2.")
    print("Exact root:  sqrt(2) = %.12f" % root)
    print()
    print("Approximate IVT (value accuracy eps):")
    print("     eps    |    N   |     x found    |    |f(x)|    | <= eps?")
    print("  " + "-" * 68)
    for eps in [1e-1, 1e-2, 1e-3, 1e-4]:
        N, x, fx = approximate_ivt(f, a, b, omega, eps)
        print(f"  {eps:.1e} | {N:6d} | {x:.12f} | {abs(fx):.3e} | {abs(fx) <= eps}")
    print()

    print("Exact IVT via the root modulus  delta -> omega(c*delta),")
    print("using the sharp conversion  |x - r| <= |f(x)| / c :")
    print("    delta   |    N   |     x found    |   |x - r|   | <= delta?")
    print("  " + "-" * 68)
    for delta in [1e-1, 1e-2, 1e-3, 1e-4]:
        N, x = constructive_ivt(f, a, b, omega, c, delta)
        print(f"  {delta:.1e} | {N:6d} | {x:.12f} | {abs(x-root):.3e} "
              f"| {abs(x - root) <= delta}")
    print()

    print("Sharpness of the constant eps/c:  for f(x) = c*x on [-1, 1] with root 0,")
    print("the point x = eps/c has |f(x)| = eps and |x - 0| = eps/c EXACTLY.")
    for cc, ee in [(1.0, 0.5), (2.0, 0.25), (0.5, 0.5)]:
        xx = ee / cc
        print(f"    c = {cc:4.2f}, eps = {ee:4.2f}:  |f(x)| = {abs(cc*xx):.4f},"
              f"  |x - r| = {abs(xx):.4f},  eps/c = {ee/cc:.4f}")
    print("  So no factor kappa < 1 can improve the bound.")
    print()

    print("Bracketing (NO non-degeneracy hypothesis): the sign-change search")
    print("lands within one mesh of a genuine root.")
    print("       N |  mesh (b-a)/N |  |x - r|   | within one mesh?")
    print("  " + "-" * 62)
    for N in [8, 64, 512, 4096]:
        k = grid_search(f, a, b, N)
        x = grid(a, b, N, k)
        mesh = (b - a) / N
        print(f"  {N:6d} | {mesh:.10f} | {abs(x-root):.3e} | {abs(x-root) <= mesh}")


def demo_shelf() -> None:
    line("6.  The shelf family: the exact IVT has no effective solution")
    print("S_t(x) = min(x - 1, max(t, x - 2))  on [0, 3],  1-Lipschitz for every t,")
    print("with S_t(0) <= 0 <= S_t(3).  The approximate IVT applies uniformly in t.")
    print()
    print("      t     | exact root(s) | approx root (N=3000) | |S_t| at that point")
    print("  " + "-" * 76)
    for t in [1.0, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0, -0.001, -0.01, -0.1, -1.0]:
        N = 3000
        k = grid_search(lambda x, t=t: shelf(t, x), 0.0, 3.0, N)
        x = grid(0.0, 3.0, N, k)
        exact = "all of [1,2]" if t == 0.0 else f"{shelf_exact_root(t):.4f}"
        print(f"  {t:+9.4f} | {exact:>13s} | {x:20.6f} "
              f"| {abs(shelf(t, x)):.3e}")
    print()
    print("The APPROXIMATE root is found effectively for every t (all |S_t| tiny).")
    print("The EXACT root jumps from 1 to 2 as t crosses 0 -- no continuous rule")
    print("can track it, and since every constructive function is continuous, no")
    print("constructive rule can either.")
    print()
    print("Quantitative failure: EVERY selector, continuous or not, has")
    print("oscillation at least 1 on every window |t| <= eta.")
    print("      eta    | r(+min(eta,1)) | r(-min(eta,1)) | oscillation >= ")
    print("  " + "-" * 68)
    for eta in [1.0, 0.1, 1e-3, 1e-6, 1e-12]:
        s = min(eta, 1.0)
        lo, hi = shelf_exact_root(s), shelf_exact_root(-s)
        print(f"  {eta:.1e} | {lo:14.1f} | {hi:14.1f} | {abs(hi-lo):.1f}")
    print()
    print("And the missing hypothesis is identified exactly: S_0 is constant on")
    print("[1, 2], so it admits no positive slope bound --")
    print(f"    S_0(1) = {shelf(0.0, 1.0)},  S_0(2) = {shelf(0.0, 2.0)}"
          "  =>  c * 1 <= 0.")


def demo_dip() -> None:
    line("7.  Local non-constancy is not enough")
    print("D_eta(x) = min(x - 1, |x - 3| + eta)  on [0, 4]:  1-Lipschitz, unique")
    print("root x = 1, local non-constancy with the explicit modulus nu(h) = h/8.")
    print()
    print("     delta  |    eta    |  |D(3)|  |  nu(delta)/2 |  distance 3 to root")
    print("  " + "-" * 74)
    for delta in [1.0, 0.5, 0.1, 0.01]:
        eta = delta / 32.0
        print(f"  {delta:8.4f} | {eta:9.6f} | {abs(dip(eta, 3.0)):.6f} "
              f"| {delta/16:12.6f} | {abs(3.0 - 1.0):.1f}")
    print()
    print("The value at x = 3 is as small as one likes, yet x = 3 is at distance 2")
    print("from the only root.  So 'small |f|' does NOT imply 'near a root' under")

def c1_error_bar_attained() -> None:
    banner("C1", "the approximation error 1/(n+1) is exact and attained")

    def alternating(n: int) -> Q:
        return Q((-1) ** n, n + 1)

        abs(alternating(m) - alternating(n)) <= Q(1, m + 1) + Q(1, n + 1)
        for m in range(60) for n in range(60)
    )
    verdict(regular, "the sequence (-1)^n/(n+1) is regular")
    # it denotes 0, and |0 - x_n| = 1/(n+1) exactly

    verdict(attained, "every term sits at distance EXACTLY 1/(n+1) from the value 0")

def c2_diagonal_shift() -> None:
    banner("C2", "the completeness diagonal must be shifted")

    def wit(k: int, n: int) -> Q:
        return Q(1, k + 1) + (1 if k % 2 == 0 else -1) * Q(1, n + 1)

    each_regular = all(
        abs(wit(k, m) - wit(k, n)) <= Q(1, m + 1) + Q(1, n + 1)
        for k in range(12) for m in range(30) for n in range(30)
    )
    verdict(each_regular, "each member x_k is a regular sequence")

    # the denoted reals are 1/(k+1), and they form a regular sequence of reals
    seq_regular = all(
        abs(Q(1, k + 1) - Q(1, l + 1)) <= Q(1, k + 1) + Q(1, l + 1)
        for k in range(40) for l in range(40)
    )
    verdict(seq_regular, "the denoted reals 1/(k+1) form a regular sequence of reals")

    naive_gap = abs(wit(0, 0) - wit(1, 1))
    permitted = Q(1, 1) + Q(1, 2)
    verdict(naive_gap > permitted,
            f"the naive diagonal violates regularity at (0,1): "
            f"{naive_gap} > {permitted}  (excess {naive_gap - permitted})")

    shifted_regular = all(
        abs(wit(2 * m + 1, 2 * m + 1) - wit(2 * n + 1, 2 * n + 1))
        <= Q(1, m + 1) + Q(1, n + 1)
        for m in range(40) for n in range(40)
    )
    verdict(shifted_regular, "the shifted diagonal (x_{2n+1})_{2n+1} IS regular")
    print("        shifted diagonal terms:",
          [str(wit(2 * n + 1, 2 * n + 1)) for n in range(5)],
          "-> limit 0, the correct value")

def c3_root_modulus() -> None:
    banner("C3", "the root modulus eps/c is attained and unimprovable")
    print("        f(x) = c x on [-1,1]:  modulus omega(e) = e/c, slope bound exactly c,")
    print("        root r = 0, test point x = eps/c.")
    print()
    print("         c    |   eps   |  |f(x)|  |  |x - r|  |   eps/c   | equal?")
    print("      " + "-" * 63)
    all_equal = True
    for c, eps in [(1.0, 1.0), (2.0, 0.5), (0.25, 0.2), (10.0, 3.0), (0.5, 0.5)]:
        x = eps / c
        eq = math.isclose(abs(x - 0.0), eps / c, rel_tol=1e-15)
        all_equal &= eq
        print(f"      {c:6.3f} | {eps:7.3f} | {abs(c*x):8.4f} | {abs(x):9.6f} "
              f"| {eps/c:9.6f} | {eq}")
    verdict(all_equal, "the bound |x - r| <= eps/c is ATTAINED in every instance")
    print("        Hence any claim |x - r| <= kappa (eps/c) with kappa < 1 is refuted")
    print("        by c = eps = 1, f(x) = x, r = 0, x = 1:  1 <= kappa is false.")

def c4_bracketing() -> None:
    banner("C4", "the sign-change search lands within one mesh -- no hypotheses")

    cases: List[Tuple[str, Callable[[float], float], float, float, List[float]]] = [
        ("x^2 - 2 on [1,2]", lambda x: x * x - 2.0, 1.0, 2.0, [math.sqrt(2)]),
        ("sin(x) - 1/2 on [0,1]", lambda x: math.sin(x) - 0.5, 0.0, 1.0,
         [math.asin(0.5)]),
        ("shelf t=0 on [0,3]", lambda x: min(x - 1.0, max(0.0, x - 2.0)), 0.0, 3.0,
         [1.0, 1.5, 2.0]),
        ("x^3 - x - 1 on [1,2]", lambda x: x ** 3 - x - 1.0, 1.0, 2.0, [1.324717957244746]),
    ]
    print("      case                    |    N  |    mesh    |  dist to root | ok")
    print("      " + "-" * 72)
    ok_all = True
    for name, f, a, b, roots in cases:
        for N in (16, 256, 4096):
            best = 0
            for k in range(N + 1):
                if f(a + k * (b - a) / N) <= 0.0:
                    best = k
            x = a + best * (b - a) / N
            mesh = (b - a) / N
            d = min(abs(x - r) for r in roots)
            ok = d <= mesh + 1e-12
            ok_all &= ok
            print(f"      {name:23s} | {N:5d} | {mesh:10.7f} | {d:13.3e} | {ok}")
    verdict(ok_all, "location accuracy is the mesh itself, with no slope bound")

def c5_local_nonconstancy() -> None:

    print("      local non-constancy holds with the explicit modulus nu(h) = h/8.")

    print("      " + "-" * 76)

        value = abs(dip(eta, 3.0))

        ok_all &= ok
        print(f"      {delta:7.4f} | {eta:9.6f} | {value:9.6f} | {delta/16:11.6f} "

                    "from the only root")

    eta = 0.01
    worst = float("inf")
    for i in range(500):

        for h in (0.05, 0.25, 1.0):
            q = min(4.0, p + h)
            if q - p < h - 1e-12:
                continue
            best = max(abs(dip(eta, p + j * (q - p) / 80.0)) for j in range(81))
            worst = min(worst, best / (h / 8.0))
    verdict(worst >= 1.0,
            f"sampled  max|D| / nu(h)  never drops below 1 (min observed {worst:.3f})")

def c6_oscillation() -> None:
    banner("C6", "every shelf root selector jumps by at least 1")

    def shelf(t: float, x: float) -> float:
        return min(x - 1.0, max(t, x - 2.0))

    # three wildly different selectors; all must have oscillation >= 1 near 0
    selectors = {
        "step (2 below 0, 1 above)": lambda t: 2.0 if t < 0 else 1.0,
        "step (2 below 0, 1 at/above), shifted at 0": lambda t: 2.0 if t <= 0 else 1.0,
        "random-looking but valid": lambda t: 2.0 if t < 0 else (
            1.5 if t == 0 else 1.0),
    }
    ok_all = True
    for name, r in selectors.items():
        valid = all(abs(shelf(t, r(t))) < 1e-12
                    for t in [-1, -0.3, -1e-6, 0.0, 1e-6, 0.3, 1])
        oscs = []
        for eta in (1.0, 0.1, 1e-6, 1e-12):
            s = min(eta, 1.0)
            vals = [r(s), r(-s), r(0.0)]
            oscs.append(max(vals) - min(vals))
        ok = valid and all(o >= 1.0 - 1e-12 for o in oscs)
        ok_all &= ok
        print(f"      {name:44s} valid={valid}  osc={['%.1f' % o for o in oscs]}")
    verdict(ok_all, "no selector, continuous or not, has oscillation below 1 at t = 0")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- C7 --------
def c7_contraction() -> None:
    banner("C7", "the one-query contraction law and the barrier 1/2")

    c = Q(1, 2)
    oracle = lambda _p, q: c <= q

    def run(alpha: Q, beta: Q, n: int) -> List[Tuple[Q, Q]]:
        enc, out = (Q(0), Q(1)), [(Q(0), Q(1))]
        for _ in range(n):
            p, q = enc
            w = q - p
            enc = (p, p + beta * w) if oracle(p + alpha * w, p + beta * w) \
                else (p + alpha * w, q)
            out.append(enc)
        return out

    print("       alpha  |   beta  |   rho   | width after 12 calls | <= rho^12 | encloses")
    print("      " + "-" * 78)
    ok_all = True
    for alpha, beta in [(Q(1, 3), Q(2, 3)), (Q(2, 5), Q(1, 2)),
                        (Q(9, 20), Q(1, 2)), (Q(499, 1000), Q(1, 2)),
                        (Q(1, 10), Q(9, 10))]:
        rho = max(beta, 1 - alpha)
        encs = run(alpha, beta, 12)
        p, q = encs[12]
        within = (q - p) <= rho ** 12
        enclosed = p < c <= q
        above_half = rho > Q(1, 2)
        ok_all &= within and enclosed and above_half
        print(f"      {str(alpha):>7s} | {str(beta):>7s} | {float(rho):.5f} "
              f"| {float(q-p):20.3e} | {str(within):9s} | {enclosed}")
    verdict(ok_all, "width <= rho^n at every stage, enclosure preserved, rho > 1/2 always")

    print()
    print("      Approaching the barrier with alpha = 1/2 - t/2, beta = 1/2 + t/2:")
    print("            t      |   rho    | rho > 1/2")
    print("      " + "-" * 44)
    for t in [Q(1, 4), Q(1, 10), Q(1, 100), Q(1, 10000), Q(1, 10 ** 8)]:
        alpha, beta = Q(1, 2) - t / 2, Q(1, 2) + t / 2
        rho = max(beta, 1 - alpha)
        print(f"      {float(t):11.1e} | {float(rho):.8f} | {rho > Q(1,2)}")
    print("      -> 1/2 is the infimum: approached for every eta > 0, attained for none.")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- C8 --------
def c8_product_shift() -> None:
    banner("C8", "the product index shift (B_x + B_y)(n+1) is sufficient")

    def sqrt_two(n: int) -> Q:
        m = n + 1
        return Q(math.isqrt(2 * m * m), m)

    def const(v: Q) -> Callable[[int], Q]:
        return lambda _n: v

    def bound(x: Callable[[int], Q]) -> int:
        return math.ceil(abs(x(0))) + 2

    # the key arithmetic inequality  M/(M(n+1)+1) <= 1/(n+1)
    key = all(Q(M, M * (n + 1) + 1) <= Q(1, n + 1)
              for M in range(1, 40) for n in range(60))
    verdict(key, "M/(M(n+1)+1) <= 1/(n+1) for every M >= 1 -- the shift repays the bound")

    pairs = [(sqrt_two, sqrt_two, 2.0),
             (sqrt_two, const(Q(3, 2)), math.sqrt(2) * 1.5),
             (const(Q(-7, 3)), const(Q(5, 4)), -35 / 12)]
    ok_all = True
    for x, y, true_value in pairs:
        M = bound(x) + bound(y)
        prod = lambda n, x=x, y=y, M=M: x(M * (n + 1)) * y(M * (n + 1))
        reg = all(abs(prod(m) - prod(n)) <= Q(1, m + 1) + Q(1, n + 1)
                  for m in range(25) for n in range(25))
        acc = all(abs(float(prod(n)) - true_value) <= 1.0 / (n + 1) + 1e-12
                  for n in range(25))
        ok_all &= reg and acc
        print(f"      B_x + B_y = {M:3d}   regular: {reg}   within 1/(n+1) of the "
              f"true product {true_value:+.6f}: {acc}")
    verdict(ok_all, "each product is regular and denotes the classical product")

    # the bound itself
    bnd_ok = all(abs(sqrt_two(n)) <= bound(sqrt_two) for n in range(500))
    verdict(bnd_ok, f"B_x = ceil(|x_0|) + 2 = {bound(sqrt_two)} dominates |x_n| for all n")

Given a function f on [a, b] presented together with an explicit modulus of
uniform continuity omega -- i.e. |x - y| <= omega(eps) implies
|f(x) - f(y)| <= eps -- and the sign condition f(a) <= 0 <= f(b), the search
evaluates f on a uniform grid of N+1 points and returns the largest index k
with f(grid_k) <= 0.

That single index carries three separate guarantees.

  (1) Approximate root.  If the mesh (b-a)/N is at most omega(eps), then
      |f(grid_k)| <= eps.  Proof: either k = N, in which case f(b) = 0; or
      f(grid_{k+1}) > 0, and the modulus applied across one mesh gives
      f(grid_{k+1}) - f(grid_k) <= eps, so f(grid_k) >= -eps.

  (2) Bracketing -- with NO non-degeneracy hypothesis.  The pair
      (grid_k, grid_{k+1}) brackets a genuine root, so grid_k is within one
      mesh (b-a)/N of an exact zero of f.  The accuracy of the *location* is
      the mesh itself.

  (3) Exact location under a slope bound.  If additionally
      f(y) - f(x) >= c (y - x) for x <= y with c > 0, then an eps-approximate
      root lies within eps/c of the unique exact root.  Running the search
      with eps = c*delta therefore returns a point within delta of the root:
      the modulus of the root is delta |-> omega(c * delta).  The constant
      eps/c is attained (take f(x) = c x, root 0, x = eps/c), so no factor
      kappa < 1 improves it.

Complexity: N + 1 evaluations of f and N comparisons, i.e. O(N) time and O(1)
space, with N = O((b - a) / omega(eps)).  For a Lipschitz function with
constant Lip, omega(eps) = eps/Lip and the cost is O(Lip (b-a) / eps); under a
slope bound c the cost of locating the root to within delta is therefore
O(Lip (b-a) / (c delta)).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable, Optional, Tuple


def grid_point(a: float, b: float, N: int, k: int) -> float:
    """The k-th point of the uniform grid of N subintervals of [a, b]."""
    return a + k * (b - a) / N


def sign_change_index(f: Callable[[float], float], a: float, b: float, N: int) -> int:
    """Return the largest grid index k in {0, ..., N} with f(grid_k) <= 0.

    Well defined because f(a) <= 0 puts k = 0 in the candidate set.
    """
    best = 0
    for k in range(N + 1):
        if f(grid_point(a, b, N, k)) <= 0.0:
            best = k
    return best


def mesh_for_accuracy(a: float, b: float, omega: Callable[[float], float],
                      eps: float) -> int:
    """Smallest safe number of subintervals N with mesh (b-a)/N <= omega(eps)."""
    step = omega(eps)
    if step <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("the modulus must be strictly positive at eps > 0")
    return max(1, int((b - a) / step) + 1)


def approximate_root(
    f: Callable[[float], float],
    a: float,
    b: float,
    omega: Callable[[float], float],
    eps: float,
) -> Tuple[float, float, int]:
    """Approximate intermediate value theorem with explicit modulus.

    Returns (x, f(x), N) with the guarantee |f(x)| <= eps and x in [a, b].
    """
    N = mesh_for_accuracy(a, b, omega, eps)
    k = sign_change_index(f, a, b, N)
    x = grid_point(a, b, N, k)
    return (x, f(x), N)


def bracket_root(
    f: Callable[[float], float], a: float, b: float, N: int
) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Bracketing form: return an interval of length one mesh (or a single
    point at the right endpoint) that provably contains an exact root.

    Requires only f(a) <= 0 <= f(b) and continuity -- no slope bound, no
    local non-constancy.
    """
    k = sign_change_index(f, a, b, N)
    if k == N:
        return (b, b)
    return (grid_point(a, b, N, k), grid_point(a, b, N, k + 1))


def locate_root(
    f: Callable[[float], float],
    a: float,
    b: float,
    omega: Callable[[float], float],
    slope: float,
    delta: float,
) -> Tuple[float, int]:
    """Exact intermediate value theorem under a positive slope bound.

    Returns (x, N) with |x - r| <= delta for the unique root r, obtained by
    running the search at value accuracy slope * delta.  The modulus of the
    root is delta |-> omega(slope * delta).
    """
    if slope <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("the slope bound must be strictly positive")
    x, _fx, N = approximate_root(f, a, b, omega, slope * delta)
    return (x, N)


def root_modulus_bound(value_error: float, slope: float) -> float:
    """The sharp conversion  |x - r| <= |f(x)| / c  of a small value into a
    small distance.  Attained by f(x) = c x at x = |f(x)|/c."""
    return value_error / slope

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Callable

Q = Fraction
Reg = Callable[[int], Q]   # a Bishop real: n |-> x_n, with the regularity promise


def error_bar(n: int) -> Q:
    """The canonical accuracy at index n, namely 1/(n+1)."""
    return Q(1, n + 1)


def is_regular(x: Reg, upto: int = 40) -> bool:
    """Check |x_m - x_n| <= 1/(m+1) + 1/(n+1) for all index pairs below `upto`."""
    return all(
        abs(x(m) - x(n)) <= error_bar(m) + error_bar(n)
        for m in range(upto)
        for n in range(upto)
    )


def from_rational(q: Q) -> Reg:
    """The Bishop real determined by a rational constant."""
    return lambda _n: q


def negate(x: Reg) -> Reg:
    """Negation; no index shift is needed."""
    return lambda n: -x(n)


def add(x: Reg, y: Reg) -> Reg:
    """Sum, with Bishop's index shift n |-> 2n + 1."""
    return lambda n: x(2 * n + 1) + y(2 * n + 1)


def subtract(x: Reg, y: Reg) -> Reg:
    """Difference, as x + (-y)."""
    return add(x, negate(y))


def canonical_bound(x: Reg) -> int:
    """B_x = ceil(|x_0|) + 2, which dominates |x_n| for every n."""
    return math.ceil(abs(x(0))) + 2


def multiply(x: Reg, y: Reg) -> Reg:
    """Product, with index shift n |-> (B_x + B_y)(n + 1)."""
    m = canonical_bound(x) + canonical_bound(y)
    return lambda n: x(m * (n + 1)) * y(m * (n + 1))


def sqrt_two() -> Reg:
    """A computable irrational: (sqrt2)_n = isqrt(2 (n+1)^2) / (n+1).

    Pure integer arithmetic.  Regularity and correctness follow from
    s <= sqrt(2) m < s + 1 for s = isqrt(2 m^2), i.e. |s/m - sqrt(2)| <= 1/m.
    """
    def approx(n: int) -> Q:
        m = n + 1
        return Q(math.isqrt(2 * m * m), m)
    return approx


def shifted_diagonal_limit(family: Callable[[int], Reg]) -> Reg:
    """Bishop's completeness construction.

    Given a regular sequence of reals (|x_k - x_l| <= 1/(k+1) + 1/(l+1)), the
    limit is the *shifted* diagonal L_n = (x_{2n+1})_{2n+1}, which satisfies
    |L - x_k| <= 1/(k+1).  The shift cannot be dropped: for the family
    (x_k)_n = 1/(k+1) + (-1)^k/(n+1) the unshifted diagonal has
    |(x_0)_0 - (x_1)_1| = 2, exceeding the permitted 3/2.
    """
    return lambda n: family(2 * n + 1)(2 * n + 1)


def approximate_to(x: Reg, accuracy: Q) -> Q:
    """Return a rational within `accuracy` of the real denoted by x, by
    querying the sequence at the first index whose error bar is small enough."""
    if accuracy <= 0:
        raise ValueError("accuracy must be positive")
    n = max(0, math.ceil(Q(1, 1) / accuracy) - 1)
    return x(n)

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Callable, List, Tuple

Q = Fraction
Oracle = Callable[[Q, Q], bool]
Enclosure = Tuple[Q, Q]


def contraction_factor(alpha: Q, beta: Q) -> Q:
    """The exact worst-case contraction per oracle call: max(beta, 1 - alpha)."""
    if not (0 < alpha < beta < 1):
        raise ValueError("query fractions must satisfy 0 < alpha < beta < 1")
    return max(beta, 1 - alpha)


def query_step(alpha: Q, beta: Q, oracle: Oracle, enc: Enclosure) -> Enclosure:
    """One oracle call; returns the new enclosure."""
    p, q = enc
    w = q - p
    if oracle(p + alpha * w, p + beta * w):
        return (p, p + beta * w)
    return (p + alpha * w, q)


def run_search(alpha: Q, beta: Q, oracle: Oracle,
               start: Enclosure, steps: int) -> List[Enclosure]:
    """Return the list of enclosures produced by `steps` oracle calls."""
    out = [start]
    for _ in range(steps):
        out.append(query_step(alpha, beta, oracle, out[-1]))
    return out


def calls_for_accuracy(alpha: Q, beta: Q, start: Enclosure, tau: Q) -> int:
    """Number of oracle calls needed to reach an enclosure of width <= tau."""
    rho = float(contraction_factor(alpha, beta))
    w0 = float(start[1] - start[0])
    if tau <= 0:
        raise ValueError("target width must be positive")
    return max(0, math.ceil(math.log(float(tau) / w0) / math.log(rho)))


def supremum_to_accuracy(alpha: Q, beta: Q, oracle: Oracle,
                         start: Enclosure, tau: Q) -> Enclosure:
    """Iterate the search until the enclosure width is at most tau."""
    enc = start
    while enc[1] - enc[0] > tau:
        enc = query_step(alpha, beta, oracle, enc)
    return enc


def supremum_as_bishop_real(alpha: Q, beta: Q, oracle: Oracle,
                            start: Enclosure) -> Callable[[int], Q]:
    """Present the supremum as a regular sequence of rationals: the k-th
    approximation is the left endpoint of the first stage of width <= 1/(k+1)."""
    def approx(k: int) -> Q:
        return supremum_to_accuracy(alpha, beta, oracle, start, Q(1, k + 1))[0]
    return approx


def oracle_half_line(c: Q) -> Oracle:
    """A located datum for S = (-inf, c] with rational c: the decidable test
    L(p, q) = (c <= q).  True certifies the upper bound q; False gives q < c,
    so the member c itself exceeds p (as p < q < c)."""
    return lambda _p, q: c <= q


def oracle_from_upper_bound_test(is_upper: Callable[[Q], bool]) -> Oracle:
    """The classical -- and constructively unavailable -- located datum:
    decide directly whether q is an upper bound.  Its existence is exactly why
    Bishop's principle is classically equivalent to ordinary completeness."""
    return lambda _p, q: is_upper(q)

    x < y   means   there exists n with   x_n + 2/(n+1) < y_n.

A proof is therefore a natural number n, from which one reads off the
CERTIFIED RATIONAL GAP

    g_n(x, y) = y_n - x_n - 2/(n+1) > 0,   with   g_n(x, y) <= y_hat - x_hat.

The gap is not an estimate: it is a proved rational lower bound on the true
difference, because |x_hat - x_n| <= 1/(n+1) on both sides.

THE ALGORITHM.  From the witness n and its gap g:

    1. compute  m = ceil(8/g) - 1,  the smallest index with 1/(m+1) <= g/8;
    2. compare the single rational  z_m  with the midpoint (x_m + y_m)/2;
    3. if z_m >= midpoint, output "x < z" witnessed at m;
       otherwise output "z < y" witnessed at m.

CORRECTNESS.  The gap survives to index m: by the two-sided error bound,
    y_m - x_m >= (y_hat - 1/(m+1)) - (x_hat + 1/(m+1)) >= g - 2/(m+1) >= 3g/4,
and the tolerance there is small: 2/(m+1) <= g/4.  So if z_m >= (x_m+y_m)/2,
    z_m - x_m >= (y_m - x_m)/2 >= 3g/8 > g/4 >= 2/(m+1),
which is precisely the witness condition for x < z at index m.  The other case
is symmetric.  Both alternatives may be true simultaneously -- which is
exactly why the test can be effective -- but the returned one is always
correct.

The arithmetic of the proof only requires 1/(m+1) < g/6; the constant 8 buys a
clean non-strict hypothesis, and whether 6 is optimal is an open question.

Complexity: three approximation queries at index m = O(1/g) and one exact
rational comparison, i.e. O(1) oracle calls at precision proportional to the
reciprocal of the certified gap.  Note that no uniform bound on the witness
index exists: for x = 0 and y = 1/(N+1) the inequality holds but no index
n <= N certifies it, so the order is decidable eventually and never uniformly.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Callable, Optional, Tuple

Q = Fraction
Reg = Callable[[int], Q]


def error_bar(n: int) -> Q:
    """The canonical accuracy 1/(n+1) at index n."""
    return Q(1, n + 1)


def certified_gap(x: Reg, y: Reg, n: int) -> Q:
    """The rational gap g_n = y_n - x_n - 2/(n+1) read off from index n."""
    return y(n) - x(n) - 2 * error_bar(n)


def find_lt_witness(x: Reg, y: Reg, search_limit: int = 10_000) -> Optional[int]:
    """Search for a witness index n certifying x < y.

    Returns None if none is found below `search_limit`; by the non-uniformity
    theorem no bound valid for all pairs exists, so the limit is a resource
    cap and not a decision procedure.
    """
    for n in range(search_limit):
        if certified_gap(x, y, n) > 0:
            return n
    return None


def cotransitivity_index(gap: Q) -> int:
    """The smallest index m with 1/(m+1) <= gap/8."""
    if gap <= 0:
        raise ValueError("the certified gap must be positive")
    return max(0, math.ceil(Q(8, 1) / gap) - 1)


def decide_cotransitive(x: Reg, y: Reg, z: Reg, witness: int) -> Tuple[str, int, Q]:
    """Decide x < z or z < y by one rational comparison.

    Returns (verdict, index used, the certified gap of the verdict).
    """
    g = certified_gap(x, y, witness)
    m = cotransitivity_index(g)
    midpoint = (x(m) + y(m)) / 2
    if z(m) >= midpoint:
        return ("x < z", m, certified_gap(x, z, m))
    return ("z < y", m, certified_gap(z, y, m))


def locate_between_rationals(x: Reg, a: Q, b: Q) -> Tuple[str, int]:
    """Constructive location: for rationals a < b, decide a < x or x < b by one
    comparison at any index m with 4/(m+1) <= b - a.

    The classically trivial dichotomy "a < x or x <= a" is NOT available; this
    overlapping disjunction is its constructive replacement.
    """
    if a >= b:
        raise ValueError("require a < b")
    m = max(0, math.ceil(Q(4, 1) / (b - a)) - 1)
    return (("a < x", m) if x(m) >= (a + b) / 2 else ("x < b", m))


def no_uniform_witness_example(N: int) -> Tuple[Reg, Reg]:
    """A pair x < y for which no index n <= N is a witness: x = 0, y = 1/(N+1).

    For n <= N one has x_n + 2/(n+1) >= 2/(N+1) > 1/(N+1) = y_n.
    """
    return (lambda _n: Q(0), lambda _n: Q(1, N + 1))

Q = Fraction


def step(alpha: Q, beta: Q, oracle: Callable[[Q, Q], bool],
         enc: Tuple[Q, Q]) -> Tuple[Q, Q]:
    p, q = enc
    w = q - p
    if oracle(p + alpha * w, p + beta * w):
        return (p, p + beta * w)
    return (p + alpha * w, q)


def run(alpha: Q, beta: Q, oracle: Callable[[Q, Q], bool],
        start: Tuple[Q, Q], n: int) -> List[Tuple[Q, Q]]:
    out = [start]
    for _ in range(n):
        out.append(step(alpha, beta, oracle, out[-1]))
    return out

<script>
const cv = document.getElementById('cv'), ctx = cv.getContext('2d');
const cv2 = document.getElementById('cv2'), ctx2 = cv2.getContext('2d');
const A = 0, B = 3;

function shelf(t, x){ return Math.min(x - 1, Math.max(t, x - 2)); }
function exactRoot(t){ return t > 0 ? 1 : (t < 0 ? 2 : 1.5); }

// largest grid index k in {0..N} with S_t(grid_k) <= 0
function searchIndex(t, N){
  let best = 0;
  for(let k = 0; k <= N; k++){
    if(shelf(t, A + k*(B-A)/N) <= 0) best = k;
  }
  return best;
}

function px(x, w){ return 60 + (x - A)/(B - A) * (w - 100); }
function py(y, h){ return h/2 - y * (h/2 - 40) / 1.35; }

function drawMain(){
  const t = +document.getElementById('t').value;
  const N = +document.getElementById('n').value;
  const w = cv.width, h = cv.height;
  ctx.clearRect(0,0,w,h);
  ctx.fillStyle = '#0b0f19'; ctx.fillRect(0,0,w,h);

  // shelf band
  ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,200,87,.10)';
  ctx.fillRect(px(1,w), 20, px(2,w)-px(1,w), h-40);

  // axes
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#2a3446'; ctx.lineWidth = 1;
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(50, py(0,h)); ctx.lineTo(w-30, py(0,h)); ctx.stroke();
  ctx.setLineDash([4,4]);
  for(const yy of [-1,-0.5,0.5,1]){
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(50, py(yy,h)); ctx.lineTo(w-30, py(yy,h)); ctx.stroke();
  }
  ctx.setLineDash([]);
  ctx.fillStyle = '#93a1bd'; ctx.font = '13px ui-monospace,monospace';
  for(const xx of [0,1,2,3]){ ctx.fillText(xx.toFixed(0), px(xx,w)-4, py(0,h)+20); }
  ctx.fillText('S_t(x)', 14, 30); ctx.fillText('x', w-24, py(0,h)+20);

  // graph
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#4fc3f7'; ctx.lineWidth = 3;
  ctx.beginPath();
  for(let i = 0; i <= 900; i++){
    const x = A + (B-A)*i/900, y = shelf(t, x);
    if(i === 0) ctx.moveTo(px(x,w), py(y,h)); else ctx.lineTo(px(x,w), py(y,h));
  }
  ctx.stroke();

  // shelf level marker
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#ffc857'; ctx.lineWidth = 2; ctx.setLineDash([6,4]);
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(px(1,w), py(t,h)); ctx.lineTo(px(2,w), py(t,h)); ctx.stroke();
  ctx.setLineDash([]);
  ctx.fillStyle = '#ffc857'; ctx.font = '13px ui-monospace,monospace';
  ctx.fillText('shelf height t = ' + t.toFixed(3), px(1,w)+8, py(t,h)-10);

  // grid samples
  const step = Math.max(1, Math.round(N/120));
  for(let k = 0; k <= N; k += step){
    const x = A + k*(B-A)/N, y = shelf(t, x);
    ctx.fillStyle = (y <= 0) ? 'rgba(239,122,133,.75)' : 'rgba(125,223,154,.75)';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(px(x,w), py(y,h), 2.6, 0, 6.2832); ctx.fill();
  }

  // the returned point
  const k = searchIndex(t, N);
  const xk = A + k*(B-A)/N, fk = shelf(t, xk);
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#7ddf9a'; ctx.lineWidth = 2.5;
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(px(xk,w), 20); ctx.lineTo(px(xk,w), h-20); ctx.stroke();
  ctx.fillStyle = '#7ddf9a';
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(px(xk,w), py(fk,h), 6, 0, 6.2832); ctx.fill();
  ctx.font = 'bold 13px ui-monospace,monospace';
  ctx.fillText('search returns x = ' + xk.toFixed(4), px(xk,w)+10, 40);

  // exact root(s)
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#ef7a85'; ctx.lineWidth = 2.5; ctx.setLineDash([5,5]);
  if(t === 0){
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(px(1,w), py(0,h)); ctx.lineTo(px(2,w), py(0,h)); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.setLineDash([]);
    ctx.fillStyle = '#ef7a85'; ctx.font = 'bold 13px ui-monospace,monospace';
    ctx.fillText('every point of [1,2] is a root', px(1,w)+8, py(0,h)+40);
  } else {
    const r = exactRoot(t);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(px(r,w), 20); ctx.lineTo(px(r,w), h-20); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.setLineDash([]);
    ctx.fillStyle = '#ef7a85'; ctx.font = 'bold 13px ui-monospace,monospace';
    ctx.fillText('exact root ' + r.toFixed(0), px(r,w)+10, h-30);
  }

  // readouts
  const mesh = (B-A)/N;
  document.getElementById('tv').textContent = t.toFixed(3);
  document.getElementById('nv').textContent = N;
  document.getElementById('mesh').textContent = mesh.toFixed(5);
  document.getElementById('xk').textContent = xk.toFixed(5);
  document.getElementById('fv').textContent = Math.abs(fk).toExponential(3);
  document.getElementById('eps').textContent = mesh.toFixed(5) + '  (since \u03c9(\u03b5)=\u03b5)';
  document.getElementById('root').textContent = (t === 0) ? 'all of [1, 2]' : exactRoot(t).toFixed(0);
  const dist = (t === 0) ? 0 : Math.min(Math.abs(xk-1), Math.abs(xk-2), Math.abs(xk-exactRoot(t)));
  document.getElementById('dist').textContent = dist.toFixed(5);

  const okApprox = Math.abs(fk) <= mesh + 1e-12;
  const okBracket = dist <= mesh + 1e-12;
  document.getElementById('badges').innerHTML =
    '<span class="pill ' + (okApprox?'ok':'warn') + '">|S_t| \u2264 mesh: ' + okApprox + '</span> ' +
    '<span class="pill ' + (okBracket?'ok':'warn') + '">within one mesh of a root: ' + okBracket + '</span>';

  let story;
  if(Math.abs(t) < 1e-9){
    story = '<strong>The critical parameter.</strong> The shelf sits exactly at height 0, so ' +
      'every point of [1, 2] is a root and the function is <em>constant</em> there. A slope bound c ' +
      'would force c\u00b71 \u2264 S\u2080(2) \u2212 S\u2080(1) = 0, so no positive slope bound exists. This is the ' +
      'single point at which the exact theorem loses all its information.';
  } else if(t > 0){
    story = '<strong>t > 0.</strong> The shelf floats above zero, so the unique root is x = 1. ' +
      'Nudge t below zero and the root will leap to x = 2 \u2014 a jump of a full unit, however tiny ' +
      'the nudge. Meanwhile the search below keeps returning a point where |S_t| is tiny.';
  } else {
    story = '<strong>t < 0.</strong> The shelf hangs below zero, so the unique root is x = 2. ' +
      'It was x = 1 a moment ago. Every root-selecting rule, continuous or not, has oscillation ' +
      'at least 1 on every window around t = 0: the roots always lie in [1, 2] and both endpoints ' +
      'are attained arbitrarily close to the critical parameter.';
  }
  document.getElementById('story').innerHTML = story;
}

function drawTrace(){
  const N = +document.getElementById('n').value;
  const tcur = +document.getElementById('t').value;
  const w = cv2.width, h = cv2.height;
  ctx2.clearRect(0,0,w,h);
  ctx2.fillStyle = '#0b0f19'; ctx2.fillRect(0,0,w,h);

  const TX = t => 60 + (t + 0.5) * (w - 100) / 1.0;
  const TY = r => h - 40 - (r - 0.85) * (h - 70) / 1.3;

  ctx2.strokeStyle = '#2a3446'; ctx2.lineWidth = 1;
  for(const r of [1, 1.5, 2]){
    ctx2.beginPath(); ctx2.moveTo(50, TY(r)); ctx2.lineTo(w-30, TY(r)); ctx2.stroke();
    ctx2.fillStyle = '#93a1bd'; ctx2.font = '12px ui-monospace,monospace';
    ctx2.fillText(r.toFixed(1), 22, TY(r)+4);
  }
  ctx2.setLineDash([4,4]);
  ctx2.beginPath(); ctx2.moveTo(TX(0), 20); ctx2.lineTo(TX(0), h-25); ctx2.stroke();
  ctx2.setLineDash([]);
  ctx2.fillStyle = '#93a1bd';
  ctx2.fillText('t = \u22120.5', TX(-0.5)-18, h-12);
  ctx2.fillText('t = 0', TX(0)-14, h-12);
  ctx2.fillText('t = +0.5', TX(0.5)-20, h-12);

  // computed root
  ctx2.strokeStyle = '#7ddf9a'; ctx2.lineWidth = 2.5;
  ctx2.beginPath();
  let started = false;
  for(let i = 0; i <= 500; i++){
    const t = -0.5 + i/500;
    const k = searchIndex(t, N);
    const xk = A + k*(B-A)/N;
    if(!started){ ctx2.moveTo(TX(t), TY(xk)); started = true; } else ctx2.lineTo(TX(t), TY(xk));
  }
  ctx2.stroke();

  // exact root
  ctx2.strokeStyle = '#ef7a85'; ctx2.lineWidth = 2; ctx2.setLineDash([6,4]);
  ctx2.beginPath(); ctx2.moveTo(TX(-0.5), TY(2)); ctx2.lineTo(TX(-0.0005), TY(2)); ctx2.stroke();
  ctx2.beginPath(); ctx2.moveTo(TX(0.0005), TY(1)); ctx2.lineTo(TX(0.5), TY(1)); ctx2.stroke();
  ctx2.setLineDash([]);
  ctx2.strokeStyle = '#ffc857'; ctx2.lineWidth = 5;
  ctx2.beginPath(); ctx2.moveTo(TX(0), TY(1)); ctx2.lineTo(TX(0), TY(2)); ctx2.stroke();
  ctx2.fillStyle = '#ffc857'; ctx2.font = 'bold 12px ui-monospace,monospace';
  ctx2.fillText('jump of size 1', TX(0)+10, TY(1.5));

  // current marker
  if(tcur >= -0.5 && tcur <= 0.5){
    ctx2.strokeStyle = '#e8edf7'; ctx2.lineWidth = 1.5;
    ctx2.beginPath(); ctx2.moveTo(TX(tcur), 20); ctx2.lineTo(TX(tcur), h-25); ctx2.stroke();
  }
}

function redraw(){ drawMain(); drawTrace(); }
function setT(v){ document.getElementById('t').value = v; redraw(); }
function sweep(){
  let v = 0.4;
  const id = setInterval(() => {
    v -= 0.008;
    if(v < -0.4){ clearInterval(id); return; }
    document.getElementById('t').value = v; redraw();
  }, 28);
}
document.getElementById('t').addEventListener('input', redraw);
document.getElementById('n').addEventListener('input', redraw);
redraw();
</script>
</body>

  label{display:block;font-size:.8rem;color:var(--muted);margin:14px 0 6px;
        text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.6px}
  input[type=range]{width:100%;accent-color:var(--gold)}
  .val{font-family:ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;color:var(--gold)}
  .big{font-family:ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;font-size:2.1rem;font-weight:700;
       text-align:center;margin:8px 0 2px}
  .bigsub{text-align:center;color:var(--muted);font-size:.8rem;margin-bottom:10px}
  .readout{font-family:ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;font-size:.85rem;line-height:1.85}
  .k{color:var(--muted)}
  table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;font-family:ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;font-size:.8rem}
  th,td{padding:5px 6px;text-align:right;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line)}
  th{color:var(--muted);font-weight:500;text-align:right}
  td:first-child,th:first-child{text-align:left}
  .note{margin-top:14px;padding:12px 14px;border-left:3px solid var(--gold);
        background:rgba(255,200,87,.07);border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;font-size:.85rem;line-height:1.6}
  .btnrow{display:flex;gap:8px;margin-top:12px;flex-wrap:wrap}
  button{background:#212b3d;color:var(--ink);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:8px;
         padding:7px 12px;font-size:.8rem;cursor:pointer}
  button:hover{border-color:var(--gold)}
  .flag{display:inline-block;padding:3px 10px;border-radius:99px;font-size:.75rem;font-weight:600}
  .flag.good{background:rgba(87,217,154,.14);color:var(--green);border:1px solid rgba(87,217,154,.4)}
  .flag.bad{background:rgba(239,106,112,.14);color:var(--red);border:1px solid rgba(239,106,112,.4)}
</style>

<body>
<div class="wrap">
  <h1>Designing a Located Supremum Search: the Contraction Race</h1>
  <p class="sub">
    A set of reals is <strong>located</strong> when it carries an oracle L that, for rationals
    p < q, either certifies that q is an upper bound (answer <em>yes</em>) or produces a
    member of the set above p (answer <em>no</em>). Both answers can be correct at once when
    p < sup S ≤ q — and that overlap is the whole story. A search maintains a rational
    enclosure (p, q) of the supremum and queries at the fractions α < β of the current
    width w: on <em>yes</em> it keeps <span class="val">(p, p+βw)</span>, on <em>no</em> it keeps
    <span class="val">(p+αw, q)</span>. So one call shrinks the width by <strong>β</strong> or by
    <strong>1−α</strong>, and the worst case is
    <span class="val">ρ = max(β, 1−α)</span>. Bishop's trisection uses (⅓, ⅔) and gets ρ = ⅔.
    Try to beat it — and see why ½ is a wall you can approach but never touch.
  </p>

  <div class="grid">
    <div class="panel">
      <canvas id="land" width="1300" height="440"></canvas>
      <canvas id="race" width="1300" height="330" style="margin-top:14px"></canvas>
    </div>

    <div class="panel">
      <div class="big" id="rho">0.667</div>
      <div class="bigsub">worst-case contraction ρ = max(β, 1−α)</div>
      <div style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:8px"><span id="flag"></span></div>

      <label>Lower query fraction  α <span class="val" id="av">0.333</span></label>
      <input id="a" type="range" min="0.01" max="0.99" step="0.001" value="0.3333">

      <label>Upper query fraction  β <span class="val" id="bv">0.667</span></label>
      <input id="b" type="range" min="0.01" max="0.99" step="0.001" value="0.6667">

      <div class="readout" style="margin-top:12px">
        <div><span class="k">on <em>yes</em>, width ×</span> <b id="wy">0.667</b></div>
        <div><span class="k">on <em>no</em>,  width ×</span> <b id="wn">0.667</b></div>
        <div><span class="k">vs trisection ρ = 2/3:</span> <b id="cmp">—</b></div>
      </div>

      <label style="margin-top:16px">Oracle calls to reach accuracy</label>
      <table>
        <tr><th>target</th><th>this ρ</th><th>trisection</th><th>saved</th></tr>
        <tbody id="tbl"></tbody>
      </table>

      <div class="btnrow">
        <button onclick="set(1/3,2/3)">Bishop's trisection</button>
        <button onclick="set(0.4,0.5)">the 2/5, 1/2 scheme</button>
        <button onclick="set(0.49,0.5)">push toward 1/2</button>
        <button onclick="set(0.499,0.5)">push harder</button>
        <button onclick="set(0.1,0.9)">a bad choice</button>
      </div>

      <div class="note" id="verdict"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
const land = document.getElementById('land'), lc = land.getContext('2d');
const race = document.getElementById('race'), rc = race.getContext('2d');
const CVAL = 0.5;                        // sup of the worked example S = (-inf, 1/2]
const oracle = (p, q) => CVAL <= q;      // the decidable located datum

function step(a, b, enc){
  const [p, q] = enc, w = q - p;
  return oracle(p + a*w, p + b*w) ? [p, p + b*w] : [p + a*w, q];
}
function run(a, b, n){
  let enc = [0, 1]; const out = [enc];
  for(let i = 0; i < n; i++){ enc = step(a, b, enc); out.push(enc); }
  return out;
}
function rho(a, b){ return Math.max(b, 1 - a); }

function drawLandscape(){
  const a = +document.getElementById('a').value, b = +document.getElementById('b').value;
  const w = land.width, h = land.height;
  lc.clearRect(0,0,w,h);
  lc.fillStyle = '#090c12'; lc.fillRect(0,0,w,h);

  const L = 70, R = w - 60, T = 30, Bo = h - 50;
  const X = t => L + t*(R-L), Y = t => Bo - t*(Bo-T);

  // heat map of rho over the admissible triangle
  const cells = 130;
  for(let i = 0; i < cells; i++){
    for(let j = 0; j < cells; j++){
      const aa = (i + .5)/cells, bb = (j + .5)/cells;
      if(aa >= bb) continue;
      const r = rho(aa, bb);
      const s = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (r - 0.5)/0.5));
      const rr = Math.round(40 + 200*s), gg = Math.round(200 - 150*s), bl = Math.round(200 - 90*s);
      lc.fillStyle = 'rgb(' + rr + ',' + gg + ',' + bl + ')';
      lc.fillRect(X(i/cells), Y((j+1)/cells), (R-L)/cells + 1, (Bo-T)/cells + 1);
    }
  }
  // inadmissible region
  lc.fillStyle = 'rgba(9,12,18,.88)';
  lc.beginPath(); lc.moveTo(X(0), Y(0)); lc.lineTo(X(1), Y(1)); lc.lineTo(X(1), Y(0));
  lc.closePath(); lc.fill();
  lc.fillStyle = '#8fa0bd'; lc.font = '14px ui-monospace,monospace';
  lc.fillText('inadmissible: a query needs \u03b1 < \u03b2', X(0.52), Y(0.22));

  // frame + ticks
  lc.strokeStyle = '#28303f'; lc.lineWidth = 1;
  lc.strokeRect(X(0), Y(1), R-L, Bo-T);
  lc.fillStyle = '#8fa0bd'; lc.font = '13px ui-monospace,monospace';
  for(const v of [0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1]){
    lc.fillText(v.toFixed(2), X(v)-14, Bo+22);
    lc.fillText(v.toFixed(2), 18, Y(v)+5);
  }
  lc.fillText('\u03b1  (lower query fraction)', X(0.38), Bo+44);
  lc.save(); lc.translate(20, Y(0.5)+90); lc.rotate(-Math.PI/2);
  lc.fillText('\u03b2  (upper query fraction)', 0, 0); lc.restore();

  // reference points
  function dot(aa, bb, col, label){
    lc.fillStyle = col; lc.strokeStyle = '#090c12'; lc.lineWidth = 2;
    lc.beginPath(); lc.arc(X(aa), Y(bb), 7, 0, 6.2832); lc.fill(); lc.stroke();
    lc.fillStyle = '#e9eef7'; lc.font = 'bold 12px ui-monospace,monospace';
    lc.fillText(label, X(aa)+12, Y(bb)+4);
  }
  dot(1/3, 2/3, '#ef6a70', 'trisection  \u03c1=0.667');
  dot(0.4, 0.5, '#57d99a', '(2/5,1/2)  \u03c1=0.600');

  // the barrier corner
  lc.fillStyle = '#ffc857';
  lc.beginPath();
  const cx = X(0.5), cy = Y(0.5);
  for(let k = 0; k < 10; k++){
    const ang = -Math.PI/2 + k*Math.PI/5, rad = (k % 2 === 0) ? 11 : 5;
    const fx = cx + rad*Math.cos(ang), fy = cy + rad*Math.sin(ang);
    if(k === 0) lc.moveTo(fx, fy); else lc.lineTo(fx, fy);
  }
  lc.closePath(); lc.fill();
  lc.fillStyle = '#ffc857'; lc.font = 'bold 12px ui-monospace,monospace';
  lc.fillText('\u03c1 \u2192 1/2, never reached', cx - 210, cy - 14);

  // the user's choice
  lc.strokeStyle = '#e9eef7'; lc.lineWidth = 2.5;
  lc.beginPath(); lc.arc(X(a), Y(b), 10, 0, 6.2832); lc.stroke();
  lc.beginPath(); lc.moveTo(X(a)-16, Y(b)); lc.lineTo(X(a)+16, Y(b));
  lc.moveTo(X(a), Y(b)-16); lc.lineTo(X(a), Y(b)+16); lc.stroke();

  lc.fillStyle = '#e9eef7'; lc.font = 'bold 15px ui-monospace,monospace';
  lc.fillText('contraction landscape  \u03c1 = max(\u03b2, 1\u2212\u03b1)', L, 20);
}

function drawRace(){
  const a = +document.getElementById('a').value, b = +document.getElementById('b').value;
  const w = race.width, h = race.height;
  rc.clearRect(0,0,w,h);
  rc.fillStyle = '#090c12'; rc.fillRect(0,0,w,h);

  const L = 70, R = w - 40, T = 24, Bo = h - 42;
  const rows = 9;
  const X = t => L + t*(R-L);
  const Ymine = i => T + (i + .28) * (Bo-T)/rows;
  const Ytri  = i => T + (i + .68) * (Bo-T)/rows;

  const admissible = a < b;
  const mine = admissible ? run(a, b, rows) : null;
  const tri  = run(1/3, 2/3, rows);

  for(let i = 0; i <= rows; i++){
    if(i >= rows) break;
    if(mine){
      const [p, q] = mine[i];
      rc.fillStyle = '#57d99a';
      rc.fillRect(X(p), Ymine(i) - 6, Math.max(1.5, X(q) - X(p)), 11);
    }
    const [p2, q2] = tri[i];
    rc.fillStyle = 'rgba(239,106,112,.85)';
    rc.fillRect(X(p2), Ytri(i) - 6, Math.max(1.5, X(q2) - X(p2)), 11);
    rc.fillStyle = '#8fa0bd'; rc.font = '11px ui-monospace,monospace';
    rc.fillText(i, 40, Ytri(i) + 2);
  }

  rc.strokeStyle = '#ffc857'; rc.lineWidth = 2; rc.setLineDash([5,4]);
  rc.beginPath(); rc.moveTo(X(CVAL), T-4); rc.lineTo(X(CVAL), Bo); rc.stroke();
  rc.setLineDash([]);
  rc.fillStyle = '#ffc857'; rc.font = 'bold 12px ui-monospace,monospace';
  rc.fillText('sup S = 1/2', X(CVAL)+8, Bo+16);

  rc.fillStyle = '#e9eef7'; rc.font = 'bold 14px ui-monospace,monospace';
  rc.fillText('computing  sup (\u2212\u221e, 1/2]  on [0,1]:  ' +
              'every stage provably encloses the answer', L, 16);
  rc.fillStyle = '#57d99a'; rc.font = '12px ui-monospace,monospace';
  rc.fillText('\u25a0 your scheme', L, Bo+30);
  rc.fillStyle = '#ef6a70';
  rc.fillText('\u25a0 Bishop trisection', L+150, Bo+30);
  rc.fillStyle = '#8fa0bd';
  rc.fillText('oracle calls made \u2193', 14, Bo+30);
}

function update(){
  const a = +document.getElementById('a').value, b = +document.getElementById('b').value;
  document.getElementById('av').textContent = a.toFixed(3);
  document.getElementById('bv').textContent = b.toFixed(3);

  const admissible = a < b;
  const r = rho(a, b);
  document.getElementById('rho').textContent = admissible ? r.toFixed(4) : '\u2014';
  document.getElementById('rho').style.color =
    !admissible ? '#ef6a70' : (r < 2/3 ? '#57d99a' : '#ffc857');
  document.getElementById('wy').textContent = b.toFixed(4);
  document.getElementById('wn').textContent = (1-a).toFixed(4);

  document.getElementById('flag').outerHTML = admissible
    ? '<span id="flag" class="flag ' + (r < 2/3 ? 'good' : 'bad') + '">' +
      (r < 2/3 ? 'beats trisection' : 'no better than trisection') + '</span>'
    : '<span id="flag" class="flag bad">inadmissible: need \u03b1 < \u03b2</span>';

  document.getElementById('cmp').textContent = admissible
    ? (r < 2/3 ? (100*(1 - Math.log(2/3)/Math.log(r))).toFixed(1) + '% fewer calls'
               : (r > 2/3 ? 'worse' : 'identical'))
    : '\u2014';

  const rows = [];
  for(const tau of [1e-3, 1e-6, 1e-9, 1e-12]){
    const nTri = Math.ceil(Math.log(tau)/Math.log(2/3));
    const nMine = admissible ? Math.ceil(Math.log(tau)/Math.log(r)) : NaN;
    rows.push('<tr><td>' + tau.toExponential(0) + '</td><td>' +
      (admissible ? nMine : '\u2014') + '</td><td>' + nTri + '</td><td>' +
      (admissible ? (nTri - nMine) : '\u2014') + '</td></tr>');
  }
  document.getElementById('tbl').innerHTML = rows.join('');

  let v;
  if(!admissible){
    v = '<strong>Not a legitimate query.</strong> The oracle is only guaranteed to answer ' +
        'correctly for p < q, so you must query at two <em>distinct, ordered</em> points. ' +
        'Collapsing them is exactly what the barrier forbids.';
  } else if(r <= 0.5 + 1e-12){
    v = '<strong>Impossible.</strong> ρ > ½ always: if β ≤ ½ then α < β ≤ ½, so 1−α > ½.';
  } else if(r < 0.505){
    v = '<strong>You are almost at the wall.</strong> As β−α shrinks, the two query points ' +
        'converge on the midpoint and each answer nearly halves the interval. But the query ' +
        'is only legitimate while α < β, so ρ = ½ + (β−α)/2 > ½ strictly. Half is the ' +
        'infimum: approached for every η > 0, attained for none.';
  } else if(r < 2/3){
    v = '<strong>Faster than Bishop.</strong> Nothing forces the query points to be symmetric ' +
        'about the midpoint. Shifting them left trades a worse <em>no</em>-branch for a much ' +
        'better <em>yes</em>-branch, and the worst case improves. The canonical example is ' +
        '(α, β) = (2/5, 1/2), with ρ = 3/5.';
  } else {
    v = '<strong>Trisection or worse.</strong> The worst case is the larger of the two ' +
        'branches, β and 1−α, so widening the gap between the query points hurts: whichever ' +
        'branch is larger is the one an adversarial oracle will keep choosing.';
  }
  document.getElementById('verdict').innerHTML = v;

  drawLandscape();
  drawRace();
}
function set(a, b){
  document.getElementById('a').value = a;
  document.getElementById('b').value = b;
  update();
}
document.getElementById('a').addEventListener('input', update);
document.getElementById('b').addEventListener('input', update);
update();
</script>
</body>
</html>
"
    },
    {
      "title": "The Bishop Real Workbench",
      "description": "A hands-on bench for the reals of constructive analysis. The first panel plots the approximations of a chosen Bishop real -- sqrt 2 via exact integer square roots, a rational, an alternating witness sequence, or a sum or product you build -- inside the guaranteed error funnel 1/(n+1), so the meaning of the regularity condition |x_m - x_n| <= 1/(m+1) + 1/(n+1) can be read straight off the picture; the index shifts that make addition and multiplication work are shown as they are consumed. The second panel is a cotransitivity decision engine: choose two Bishop reals x < y and a third z, and the widget computes the certified rational gap at the witness index, derives the test index m with 1/(m+1) <= gap/8, performs the single midpoint comparison, and reports which of x < z or z < y it has decided together with the certificate. Shrinking the gap sends the required index to infinity, demonstrating that no uniform witness bound can exist.",
      "html": "<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">

<body>
<div class="wrap">
  <h1>Bishop Real Workbench</h1>
  <p class="sub">
    A Bishop real is a sequence of rationals carrying its own modulus:
    <span class="val">|x<sub>m</sub> − x<sub>n</sub>| ≤ 1/(m+1) + 1/(n+1)</span>.
    From that single inequality follows the estimate that makes the whole theory usable:
    <span class="val">|x̂ − x<sub>n</sub>| ≤ 1/(n+1)</span> — <em>the index is the error bar</em>.
    Below, the left panel shows a computable irrational sitting inside its guaranteed funnel;
    the right panel runs the constructive order, where an inequality is not an assertion but a
    <em>witness index</em> from which a rational lower bound on the gap can be read off.
  </p>

  <div class="grid">
    <!-- ---------------- funnel ---------------- -->
    <div class="panel">
      <h2>1  ·  The funnel: approximations inside their own error bars</h2>
      <canvas id="funnel" width="820" height="420"></canvas>

      <label>Highest index shown  <span class="val" id="nmaxv">40</span></label>
      <input id="nmax" type="range" min="6" max="120" step="1" value="40">

      <label>Sequence</label>
      <select id="seq">
        <option value="sqrt2">√2   (n-th term = ⌊√(2(n+1)²)⌋ / (n+1), integer arithmetic)</option>
        <option value="sqrt3">√3   (n-th term = ⌊√(3(n+1)²)⌋ / (n+1))</option>
        <option value="pi">π  (n-th term = ⌊π(n+1)⌋ / (n+1))</option>
      </select>

      <div class="readout" style="margin-top:10px">
        <div><span class="k">query index n =</span> <b id="qn">9</b></div>
        <div><span class="k">x_n =</span> <b id="qv">—</b></div>
        <div><span class="k">guaranteed error ≤ 1/(n+1) =</span> <b id="qe">—</b></div>
        <div><span class="k">actual error =</span> <b id="qa">—</b></div>
      </div>
      <label>Query index  <span class="val" id="qiv">9</span></label>
      <input id="qi" type="range" min="0" max="120" step="1" value="9">

      <div class="note">
        No quantifier is dodged here. Ask for the term at index 999 and you receive a rational
        that is <em>provably</em> within 1/1000 of the answer — no further computation, no
        appeal to a limit you cannot locate. That is the entire difference between a Cauchy
        sequence and a regular one.
      </div>
    </div>

    <!-- ---------------- order ---------------- -->
    <div class="panel">
      <h2>2  ·  The order: witnesses and cotransitivity</h2>
      <canvas id="order" width="820" height="300"></canvas>

      <label>x  <span class="val" id="xv">0.000</span></label>
      <input id="x" type="range" min="-1" max="1" step="0.001" value="0">
      <label>y  <span class="val" id="yv">0.333</span></label>
      <input id="y" type="range" min="-1" max="1" step="0.001" value="0.333">
      <label>third real z  <span class="val" id="zv">0.100</span></label>
      <input id="z" type="range" min="-1" max="1" step="0.001" value="0.1">

      <div class="verdict" id="verdict">—</div>

      <div class="readout">
        <div><span class="k">witness index n for x < y =</span> <b id="wn">—</b></div>
        <div><span class="k">certified rational gap g =</span> <b id="gg">—</b></div>
        <div><span class="k">decision index m = ⌈8/g⌉−1 =</span> <b id="mm">—</b></div>
        <div><span class="k">midpoint (x_m+y_m)/2 =</span> <b id="mid">—</b></div>
        <div><span class="k">z_m =</span> <b id="zm">—</b></div>
      </div>

      <div class="btnrow">
        <button onclick="setxyz(0,0.5,0.05)">z near x</button>
        <button onclick="setxyz(0,0.5,0.25)">z at the midpoint</button>
        <button onclick="setxyz(0,0.5,0.45)">z near y</button>
        <button onclick="setxyz(0,0.02,0.01)">a tiny gap</button>
      </div>

      <div class="note">
        Classically, x < y gives "x < z or z < y" for free. Constructively the
        disjunction must be <em>decided</em>, and it can be: the gap g read off from the witness
        determines an index m at which one comparison of rationals settles it. Both alternatives
